questionText: What is an embedded server in Spring Boot and why is it useful?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can define an embedded server by ownership and lifecycle, explain the executable deployment benefit, and distinguish it from architecture style and external WAR deployment.
inScope: Default embedded Tomcat for Spring MVC
outOfScope: A claim that embedded always means physically inside a JAR
A claim that embedded deployment creates a microservice

claims.statement: An embedded server is supplied on the application classpath and created, started, and stopped as part of the Spring Boot web application lifecycle.
In Spring Boot 3.3.1, spring-boot-starter-web brings the Tomcat starter by default for a servlet web application.
The Spring Boot build plugin can package application classes and runtime dependencies into an executable archive launched with java -jar.

examples.title: Java 17 Boot application with one status endpoint

validation.command: Review the focused example against Java 17 and Spring Boot 3.3.1 APIs and configuration metadata
validation.expected: The imports, main method, controller mapping, and Java syntax form a focused valid example when the web starter is present

visuals.title: Dependency, context, server startup, request, and shutdown flow

notes: The answer defines embedded by application ownership rather than claiming the server only exists physically inside a packaged JAR.

review.notes: Ownership, default server, executable packaging, and external-deployment boundary were checked against the official Spring Boot 3.3 documentation. Java example remains honestly marked manual review.
